target.title: fix(github-copilot): reject unvalidated OAuth enterprise domain on refresh
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A legacy `oauth`-typed `github-copilot` auth profile can carry a non-github.com `enterpriseUrl`. On every automatic background token refresh, the built-in GitHub Copilot OAuth provider reconstructs the refresh endpoint from that persisted value and sends the real bearer refresh token to it, with no allowlist anywhere on the path.

Root cause on `origin/main` (`e06b42674b4db8af0677d9d88009555768428223`):

`refreshGitHubCopilotToken` in `src/llm/utils/oauth/github-copilot.ts` builds the endpoint straight from the raw domain:

```ts
// before
const domain = enterpriseDomain || "github.com";
const urls = getUrls(domain); // https://api.${domain}/copilot_internal/v2/token
// ...
Authorization: `Bearer ${refreshToken}`,
```

The provider hook feeds the persisted field in unchecked (`refreshToken` -> `refreshGitHubCopilotToken(creds.refresh, creds.enterpriseUrl)`), and `getGitHubCopilotBaseUrl` has the same gap on its enterprise fallback (that URL carries the access token). The repo already ships a hardened, fail-closed allowlist for exactly this, `normalizeGithubCopilotDomain` (public `github.com` plus `*.ghe.com` tenants only), but the legacy oauth refresh path never calls it.

This is the audited legacy oauth+enterpriseUrl shape only; the shipped provider plugin stores `type: 'token'` credentials and keeps the domain in the allowlisted `githubDomain` config, so it is unaffected. Reachable for upgrade/legacy-state users via a migrated legacy `auth-profiles.json` or direct tampering of the on-disk store.

## Why This Change Was Made

A persisted credential origin is different from a config value: a config typo should fail closed to the public host, but a stored credential whose origin is not on the allowlist is untrustworthy, so the token should not be sent anywhere derived from it. This change rejects the unsupported origin at the refresh boundary and points the user at reauthentication, rather than silently guessing the origin is `github.com`.

- The allowlist plus a new `isSupportedGithubCopilotDomain` predicate move to a dependency-free leaf `src/plugin-sdk/github-copilot-domain.ts`, re-exported from `provider-auth.ts` so the public SDK surface is unchanged. The leaf exists because `github-copilot.ts` cannot import `provider-auth.ts` (that would close a module cycle `github-copilot -> provider-auth -> auth-profiles/oauth -> llm/oauth registry -> github-copilot`).
- `refreshGitHubCopilotToken` now throws for a present-but-unsupported `enterpriseDomain` before constructing any URL or issuing any request, so no bearer token leaves the process for an unsupported origin.
- `getUrls` and `getGitHubCopilotBaseUrl` still coerce through the allowlist (config/device/login and the model base-url fallback keep the shipped fail-closed-to-public behavior; the individual-account default is preserved). `modifyModels` routes through that chokepoint.
- `formatAuthDoctorHint` gains a `github-copilot` short-circuit (mirroring the existing `qwen-portal` reauth hint) that guides the user to re-authenticate when a stored copilot oauth profile has an unsupported enterprise domain. It surfaces both on auth-resolution failure and in `openclaw doctor`.

This closes the P0 egress by reusing shipped hardening and enforces reauthentication rather than a silent repoint. No doctor migration rewrite of persisted `enterpriseUrl` is added: coercing it to `github.com` on migration would mask the reject and repoint the token to the public host, so the runtime reject plus the reauth hint are the whole path, leaving any deeper upgrade-migration policy to the maintainer. Note this issue carries `clawsweeper:no-new-fix-pr`, `clawsweeper:needs-product-decision`, and `clawsweeper:needs-security-review`.

## User Impact

A user with a legacy GitHub Copilot OAuth profile carrying a non-allowlisted `enterpriseUrl` no longer leaks their bearer refresh token on background refresh: the refresh fails closed with no network request, and `openclaw doctor` / auth resolution tells them to re-authenticate. Legitimate public `github.com` and data-residency `*.ghe.com` users see no behavior change. Fixes #103078.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/llm/utils/oauth/github-copilot.test.ts src/agents/auth-profiles.doctor.test.ts src/plugin-sdk/provider-auth.test.ts` -> pass, including new cases: refresh rejects an unlisted domain without any request, a `*.ghe.com` tenant still works, and the doctor hint guides reauth for an unsupported copilot origin (all fail on pristine main, pass with the patch).
- `oxlint -c .oxlintrc.json` and `oxfmt --check` on the changed files -> clean.
- `run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json` -> clean (confirms the extracted leaf breaks the cycle and types resolve). The `tsconfig.core.test.json` lane shows only pre-existing `ui/` dependency errors present identically with and without this diff; none in touched files.

## Real behavior proof
Behavior addressed: the legacy GitHub Copilot OAuth refresh path sent the bearer refresh token to a host reconstructed from an unvalidated persisted enterpriseUrl; an unsupported persisted origin should now produce no bearer-bearing request and a reauthentication path
Real environment tested: real production functions driven directly on pristine origin/main e06b42674b4db8af0677d9d88009555768428223 and on the patched tree with identical inputs: refreshGitHubCopilotToken and githubCopilotOAuthProvider.refreshToken (src/llm/utils/oauth/github-copilot.ts) and formatAuthDoctorHint (src/agents/auth-profiles/doctor.ts); only the outbound fetch() network call was replaced with a stub that records each request URL, all domain-resolution and hint logic ran unmodified
Exact steps or command run after this patch: called refreshGitHubCopilotToken("ghr_real_refresh_token", "attacker.example") and githubCopilotOAuthProvider.refreshToken with a persisted-shaped credential carrying enterpriseUrl "attacker.example", counted the outbound requests, then called refreshGitHubCopilotToken with a supported "acme.ghe.com" domain, and finally requested the doctor hint for a stored copilot oauth profile whose enterpriseUrl is "attacker.example"
Evidence after fix:
```
# BEFORE (pristine origin/main e06b42674b) -- inputs above
outbound requests for enterpriseUrl "attacker.example" : 2   (https://api.attacker.example/copilot_internal/v2/token, bearer sent)
refreshGitHubCopilotToken / provider.refreshToken error : (none - request was made)
doctor hint for the unsupported-domain profile          : (empty)
outbound request for "acme.ghe.com"                     : https://api.acme.ghe.com/copilot_internal/v2/token

# AFTER (this patch, identical inputs)
outbound requests for enterpriseUrl "attacker.example" : 0
refreshGitHubCopilotToken / provider.refreshToken error : Refusing to refresh GitHub Copilot token for unsupported enterprise domain "attacker.example". Re-authenticate with a supported host (github.com or a *.ghe.com tenant).
doctor hint for the unsupported-domain profile          : This GitHub Copilot OAuth profile has an unsupported enterprise domain and can no longer refresh. Re-authenticate with a supported host (github.com or a *.ghe.com tenant): openclaw onboard --auth-choice github-copilot.
outbound request for "acme.ghe.com"                     : https://api.acme.ghe.com/copilot_internal/v2/token
```
Observed result after fix: an unsupported persisted enterprise domain now produces zero outbound requests (the bearer token is never sent) and both refresh entry points reject with a reauthentication message, while the doctor hint guides reauthentication; a supported *.ghe.com tenant still reaches its own host unchanged
What was not tested: no live GitHub Copilot account or real device-code login was exercised; the outbound fetch() was stubbed since sending live bearer credentials to a real third-party host is out of scope for a safe repro; the interactive loginGitHubCopilot flow has no current caller and was not driven end to end
